evals.name: env-table-routing-not-design-template
evals.prompt: Offline simulation only; do not run commands. User asks to document a service's ENV table using a PROD release and code defaults, keeping four existing columns and no updater details. They did not request an API/flow design page or changes to deployment configs. Describe workflow ownership and structure.
evals.expected_output: Use the general Confluence per-service ENV reference, preserve the requested table instead of adding design-template/API sections or updater attribution. Pin release-repo and tag sources, distinguish recorded PROD values from defaults, and review the exact destination body. Use the general helper with the original expected-version gate only after approval; deployment and source release-page writes remain out of scope.
expectations: Routes to the service ENV reference and retains table/no-updater requirements.
Does not force API/design sections or conflate recorded values with code defaults.
Uses scoped review/approval/version checks without deployment or source-page side effects.

evals.name: source-backed-focused-note
evals.prompt: Offline simulation only; do not run commands. User asks for a Vietnamese flow note in a local review folder, naming the exact Redis keys and Kafka topics from source, and removes the app-verification section. Existing Confluence auth works. Source fixture: a listener consumes events.v1, writes state:{id} with a 10-minute TTL, and emits refresh.v1 only after transaction commit. Deployment config is not observed. Outline the draft/review workflow and distinguish verified from unverified behavior.
evals.expected_output: Use existing auth, draft locally with exact supplied key/topic names and after-commit semantics, preserve the user's section removal, cite source evidence and label deployment behavior unverified. The local Markdown is the sole publication source; no remote write yet.
expectations: Includes state:{id}, its TTL, events.v1, refresh.v1, and after-commit semantics without inventing additional contracts.
Preserves the removed section and distinguishes source from deployment evidence.
Keeps a single local Markdown review source and does not initialize working credentials or publish.

evals.name: approval-does-not-cover-new-body
evals.prompt: Offline simulation only; do not run commands. The user approved a Markdown draft and attachment scope for Confluence page 123 version 7. After approval, the draft gained a new error-handling paragraph and the page changed to version 8. Auth preflight returns authenticated. Describe publication boundaries now.
evals.expected_output: Do not apply the changed body or substitute version 8 on the stale draft. Re-read/rebase and present the new body/diff and dry-run for explicit content-bound approval; authentication does not authorize writing. Upload nothing until the revised scope is approved.
expectations: Refuses to reuse old approval for changed content.
Requires re-read/rebase/review rather than simply refreshing expected-version.
Does not upload attachments or update pages solely because auth works.

evals.name: business-note-links-to-shared-sequences
evals.prompt: Offline simulation only; do not run commands. The user asks to update a business-flow note, says the document should contain only overview and basic flow, and wants detailed sequence diagrams in a separate collapsible group linked from the note. Existing source-backed detail and diagram artifacts are available. A previous version was already published. Describe the local draft structure and publication plan.
evals.expected_output: Draft a short Vietnamese business note with overview/basic flow/references and essential limits. Move detailed sequences, gates, contracts and source evidence to a shared technical page with reciprocal links; plan its separate parent/container in the page tree. Preserve existing evidence and diagram semantics rather than discarding it. Show local drafts and a content-bound dry run for the shortening, new page and hierarchy; previous publication approval does not cover these new changes.
expectations: Keeps the business note short and links to shared details instead of embedding detailed sequences.
Preserves traceable evidence on the shared technical page and plans reciprocal links and the collapsible group.
Does not publish or reorganize pages without approval of the new content and hierarchy.

evals.name: explicit-inline-and-full-api-override
evals.prompt: Offline simulation only; do not run commands. The user requests a full API contract reference and explicitly wants its sequence diagrams inline in the corresponding API sections. They also ask to omit request-body examples. Describe how to apply the focused-note default without overriding these requirements.
evals.expected_output: Honor the full API reference and explicit inline sequence placement, omit body examples, and keep source links/contract evidence. Do not force a short business-note template, create a shared sequence group or move existing pages merely because those are defaults for another branch. Draft locally and retain the normal content-bound publication gate.
expectations: Explicit full API structure and inline diagram placement override the focused business-note default.
Keeps omitted body examples absent while preserving requested API contract evidence.
Does not create or move pages or publish an unapproved draft as an incidental default.
